readings: The shutter is open. The top of the tree throws its light below the hole. On the near screen the image is small and upside down.
The shutter covers the hole. The tree is still standing outside. There is no tree on the near screen.
The open hole lets the same rays travel farther. They meet the far screen farther apart. The upside-down tree fills more paper.
The far screen stays dark behind the closed shutter. Moving the screen changes where the rays could land. It cannot let them in.

invitation: Set the ball between the lamp and the reading screen
controls: Bring the ball back to centre
Stand at the edge of the screen
Stand at the centre of the screen
readings: You stand directly behind the ball. It cuts off the lamp. The side of the screen beside you is still lit.
From the centre you see the lamp again. The ball's shadow moved sideways. A watcher standing there would give a different report.
From the side you can see the lamp. The centre mark is dark although you are standing in light.
At the side mark you now stand behind the moved ball. The centre is clear. Both reports describe the same arrangement.

invitation: Slide the beads on the trader’s purse cord
controls: Add two coins to the purse
Tie a three-coin debt to the cord
readings: The purse is empty and the cord carries no debt. The keeper starts at zero.
Two coins are in the purse. The cord has no debt knots. The owner's balance stands two beads above zero.
An empty purse hangs over three debt knots. You can point to a balance below zero without putting a negative coin in anybody's hand.
Two coins, three owed. The owner can pay out the coins and still owe one. Counting only the purse would give the visitor a very different answer.

invitation: Splice the scrape into a pocket sound reel
controls: Slip the reel by one beat
readings: The little reel marks a low scrape, a higher ring, then two empty beats. The lamp pulses at the start of the strip.
A knock enters on the third beat. The fourth beat stays empty. The room has become part of the phrase.
The scrape starts on the second beat and the ring on the third. The lamp hasn't moved. The same two sounds lean against it differently.
Scrape, ring and knock start one beat late. The knock lands just before the lamp restarts. The gap has moved to the front.
